describes: §8.3 asymmetric signing — ES256 (ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256) verification
note: ECDSA signing is RANDOMIZED, so — like TC-ENV — these are VERIFY-direction known-answer vectors, not sign-direction ones. A conforming verifier MUST reproduce every expect_verify below. The signature covers the §6 RFC 8785 canonical form of `payload` with the `field` omitted (see signing_input). Keys and signatures are base64. An implementation proves the sign direction by round-tripping its own output; it proves interop by verifying these fixed vectors.

vectors.description: A genuine ES256 signature over the canonical mandate verifies
The same signature does NOT verify once a term is changed (500 → 5000000) — sign-what-you-see
A corrupted signature does not verify
